title: Glede seg til eller være glad for — anticipation and appreciation
goal: Use glede seg til for anticipation and være glad for for satisfaction, appreciation, or gratitude about an existing fact.

objectives.statement: Use glede seg til for anticipation and være glad for for satisfaction, appreciation, or gratitude about an existing fact.

spans.value: Sara and Jonas are meeting at Oslo Central Station on Friday afternoon. They are travelling to a cabin near Lillehammer. Sara planned the trip, while Jonas bought the food.

blocks.translation: I’m looking forward to the weekend.

spans.value: Jeg også. Jeg gleder meg til å komme meg ut av byen.

blocks.translation: Me too. I’m looking forward to getting out of the city.

spans.value: Og jeg er glad for at du kjøpte maten. Jeg hadde ikke tid i går.

blocks.translation: And I’m glad that you bought the food. I didn’t have time yesterday.

spans.value: Det går bra. Jeg er glad for at du bestilte hytta.

blocks.translation: That’s fine. I’m glad that you booked the cabin.

spans.value: Gleder du deg til skituren i morgen?

blocks.translation: Are you looking forward to the ski trip tomorrow?

spans.value: Ja, men jeg er også glad for det varme tøyet mitt. Det blir kaldt!

blocks.translation: Yes, but I’m also glad to have my warm clothes. It’s going to be cold!

spans.value: Toget går om ti minutter. Jeg er glad for at vi kom tidlig.

blocks.translation: The train leaves in ten minutes. I’m glad that we arrived early.

spans.value: Two different kinds of positive feeling appear in this conversation. Sara and Jonas feel anticipation about the weekend, leaving the city, and tomorrow’s ski trip. They use
. They also appreciate things that are already true: Jonas bought the food, Sara booked the cabin, Jonas has warm clothes, and they arrived early. For these existing facts, they use
when someone feels happy or excited about something that is coming. A natural English translation is often
is a reflexive verb. The reflexive pronoun changes with the subject:

no.value: Jeg gleder meg til turen.

en.value: I’m looking forward to the trip.

no.value: Du gleder deg til turen.

en.value: You’re looking forward to the trip.

no.value: Hun gleder seg til turen.

en.value: She’s looking forward to the trip.

no.value: Vi gleder oss til turen.

en.value: We’re looking forward to the trip.

no.value: Dere gleder dere til turen.

en.value: You’re looking forward to the trip.

no.value: De gleder seg til turen.

en.value: They’re looking forward to the trip.

spans.value: . Do not leave out the reflexive pronoun, and do not replace

no.value: Jeg gleder meg til konserten.

en.value: I’m looking forward to the concert.

no.value: Barna gleder seg til ferien.

en.value: The children are looking forward to the holiday.

no.value: Vi gleder oss til middag.

en.value: We’re looking forward to dinner.

spans.value: followed by a verb when you are looking forward to doing something:

no.value: Jeg gleder meg til å møte familien din.

en.value: I’m looking forward to meeting your family.

no.value: Hun gleder seg til å begynne i den nye jobben.

en.value: She’s looking forward to starting the new job.

no.value: Vi gleder oss til å se dere igjen.

en.value: We’re looking forward to seeing you again.

spans.value: The event does not need to be far in the future. It only needs to be something viewed as still ahead.

no.value: Jeg gleder meg til kaffen etter møtet.

en.value: I’m looking forward to the coffee after the meeting.

no.value: Han gleder seg til å legge seg.

en.value: He’s looking forward to going to bed.

no.value: Gleder dere dere til filmen i kveld?

en.value: Are you looking forward to the film tonight?

sections.title: Appreciating what is already true: være glad for

spans.value: when someone is satisfied with, appreciates, or feels grateful for something that is already a fact.
In the station dialogue, the food has already been bought:

no.value: Sara er glad for at Jonas kjøpte maten.

en.value: Sara is glad that Jonas bought the food.

spans.value: The cabin has already been booked:

no.value: Jonas er glad for at Sara bestilte hytta.

en.value: Jonas is glad that Sara booked the cabin.

spans.value: Sara and Jonas are already at the station:

no.value: De er glade for at de kom tidlig.

en.value: They are glad that they arrived early.

spans.value: These sentences do not express anticipation. They express a positive reaction to an existing situation.
can be followed by a noun:

no.value: Jeg er glad for hjelpen.

en.value: I’m grateful for the help.

no.value: Hun er glad for den nye leiligheten sin.

en.value: She is happy with her new apartment.

no.value: Vi er glade for resultatet.

en.value: We are pleased with the result.

spans.value: It can also be followed by

no.value: Jeg er glad for at du er her.

en.value: I’m glad that you are here.

no.value: Han er glad for at bussen kom.

en.value: He is glad that the bus arrived.

no.value: Vi er glade for at alle har det bra.

en.value: We are glad that everyone is doing well.

spans.value: The English translation depends on the context.
may all be appropriate. The Norwegian expression remains
Compare appreciation of a thing with appreciation of a fact:

no.value: Jeg er glad for hjelpen.

en.value: I’m grateful for the help.

no.value: Jeg er glad for at du hjalp meg.

en.value: I’m glad that you helped me.

spans.value: Both refer to help that is real or has already happened. The second sentence states the fact more fully.

sections.title: Checkpoint: connect feelings to existing facts

spans.value: Use brief descriptions of completed actions or present circumstances to express why a person appreciates them. Examples include Jonas’s shopping, Sara’s booking, warm clothing, and arriving at the station on time.
Both expressions describe positive feelings, but they look in different directions.

no.value: Jeg gleder meg til besøket.

en.value: I’m looking forward to the visit.

no.value: Jeg er glad for besøket.

en.value: I’m pleased about the visit.

no.value: Vi gleder oss til at Anna kommer i morgen.

en.value: We’re looking forward to Anna coming tomorrow.

no.value: Vi er glade for at Anna kan komme.

en.value: We’re glad that Anna can come.

no.value: Han gleder seg til den nye jobben.

en.value: He’s looking forward to the new job.

no.value: Han er glad for den nye jobben.

en.value: He’s happy with the new job.

spans.value: The surrounding context determines what the speaker means. Consider the new job:

no.value: Erik begynner i den nye jobben på mandag. Han gleder seg til den.

en.value: Erik starts the new job on Monday. He’s looking forward to it.

spans.value: The job is still ahead, so

no.value: Erik har jobbet der i to måneder. Han er glad for den nye jobben.

en.value: Erik has worked there for two months. He is happy with the new job.

spans.value: The job is now part of his life, so
The same contrast appears with a visit:

no.value: Bestemor kommer neste helg, og jeg gleder meg til besøket.

en.value: Grandma is coming next weekend, and I’m looking forward to the visit.

no.value: Bestemor kunne komme tidligere enn planlagt, og jeg er glad for det.

en.value: Grandma was able to come earlier than planned, and I’m glad about that.

spans.value: In the first sentence, the visit is anticipated. In the second, the speaker appreciates an existing fact about the visit.

Compare paired situations about the same topic. In one, the speaker anticipates an experience; in the other, the speaker appreciates an arrangement, result, or current circumstance. A confirmed future event can still support either expression, so attend to the speaker’s stance.
These expressions are useful in everyday conversation because they invite different kinds of answers.

no.value: Gleder du deg til helgen?

en.value: Are you looking forward to the weekend?

no.value: Ja, jeg gleder meg til å slappe av.

en.value: Yes, I’m looking forward to relaxing.

no.value: Gleder barna seg til turen?

en.value: Are the children looking forward to the trip?

no.value: Ja, de gleder seg til å ta toget.

en.value: Yes, they’re looking forward to taking the train.

spans.value: To ask about appreciation or satisfaction:

no.value: Er du glad for den nye sykkelen?

en.value: Are you happy with the new bicycle?

no.value: Ja, jeg er glad for at den er så lett.

en.value: Yes, I’m glad that it is so light.

no.value: Er dere glade for hjelpen?

en.value: Are you grateful for the help?

no.value: Ja, vi er glade for at naboene kunne hjelpe oss.

en.value: Yes, we’re glad that the neighbours could help us.

spans.value: Notice that the question often guides the time perspective.
asks what someone appreciates or feels satisfied with.
Respond to short questions about anticipation or appreciation using the question’s subject and situation. Include a plausible reason or detail without changing the intended time perspective.
Using være glad for for a future event when anticipation is intended
Less natural for the intended meaning:

no.value: Jeg er glad for festen i morgen.

en.value: I’m glad about the party tomorrow.

no.value: Jeg gleder meg til festen i morgen.

en.value: I’m looking forward to the party tomorrow.

spans.value: The first sentence could make sense if the speaker appreciates the fact that the party has been arranged. It does not clearly express looking forward to attending it.
Using glede seg til for gratitude
cannot express gratitude for something that has already happened.

no.value: Jeg gleder meg til hjelpen du ga meg.

en.value: I’m looking forward to the help you gave me.

no.value: Jeg er glad for hjelpen du ga meg.

en.value: I’m grateful for the help you gave me.

spans.value: The help is already a fact, so

no.value: Vi gleder til ferien.

en.value: We’re looking forward to the holiday.

no.value: Vi gleder oss til ferien.

en.value: We’re looking forward to the holiday.

spans.value: The pronoun must match the subject:

no.value: Hun gleder seg for konserten.

en.value: She’s looking forward to the concert.

no.value: Hun gleder seg til konserten.

en.value: She’s looking forward to the concert.

no.value: Jeg er glad til at du kom.

en.value: I’m glad that you came.

no.value: Jeg er glad for at du kom.

en.value: I’m glad that you came.

spans.value: Learn each expression together with its preposition:
An announcement says that Sara and Jonas’s train is delayed by fifteen minutes.
Jeg er glad for at vi har god tid.

blocks.translation: I’m glad that we have plenty of time.

spans.value: Ja. Da kan vi kjøpe kaffe. Jeg gleder meg til å drikke en kopp kaffe på toget.

blocks.translation: Yes. Then we can buy coffee. I’m looking forward to drinking a cup of coffee on the train.

spans.value: Jeg er glad for at kiosken fortsatt er åpen.

blocks.translation: I’m glad that the kiosk is still open.

spans.value: Og jeg gleder meg til å gå på ski i morgen.

blocks.translation: And I’m looking forward to skiing tomorrow.

spans.value: The scene contains both kinds of positive feeling. They appreciate existing facts: they have enough time, and the kiosk is open. They also anticipate what comes next: drinking coffee on the train and skiing tomorrow.
Retell the station situation from Sara’s or Jonas’s perspective. Express both anticipation of what still lies ahead and appreciation of facts that help the journey go well.

prompt.value: Sara finds the note and tells someone what it says. Choose the sentence that fits.

options.text: Jonas er glad for at han skal drikke kaffe på toget i morgen.
options.why: Dette framstiller planen som noe han setter pris på, ikke som en opplevelse han gleder seg til.

options.text: Jeg gleder meg til å drikke kaffe på toget i morgen.
options.why: Dette endrer subjektet fra Jonas til den som snakker.

options.text: Jonas gleder seg til å drikke kaffe på toget i morgen.
options.why: Kaffeopplevelsen ligger fortsatt fram i tid, og Jonas trenger det refleksive pronomenet seg.

stem.value: «Kaffe på toget i morgen. Kan ikke vente!»

prompt.value: Choose the pair of sentences that fits the situation.

options.text: Sara er glad for skituren i morgen. Hun er glad for at hun har varme klær i sekken.
options.why: The first sentence does not express Sara’s stated anticipation of skiing.

options.text: Sara er glad for at hun skal gå på ski i morgen. Hun gleder seg til å ha varme klær.
options.why: The expressions assign appreciation to the future plan and anticipation to clothes already packed.

options.text: Sara gleder seg til å gå på ski i morgen. Hun gleder seg til de varme klærne.
options.why: The second sentence treats clothes already packed in the bag as a future experience.

options.text: Sara gleder seg til å gå på ski i morgen. Hun er glad for at hun har varme klær i sekken.
options.why: The skiing is anticipated, while the packed clothes are an existing fact she appreciates.

stem.value: Sara says, «Jeg gleder meg til å stå på ski i morgen.» She has already packed warm clothes.

prompt.value: Message from Nora: «Du skal reise videre og drikke kaffe på toget. Hva gleder du deg til? Sara har fått hjelp, og reisen er bestilt. Hva er hun glad for?» Reply to Nora in Norwegian. Answer both questions with one relevant fact each, and use both «glede seg til» and «være glad for».

payload.judge_prompt: Check the reply against criteria answer-both, relevant-details, expression-choice, and reflexive-agreement. All listed criteria are gating.

criteria.instruction: Answers what the writer anticipates on the journey and what Sara appreciates about the completed help or booking.
Gives one relevant reason or detail for each answer without contradicting the message.
Uses glede seg til for anticipation and være glad for for appreciation.
Uses a reflexive pronoun that agrees with its subject when expressing anticipation.

prompt.value: The train is 15 minutes late. Sara and Jonas have plenty of time, the kiosk is open, and they can have coffee on the train. Tomorrow they are going skiing. Write a message from Sara or Jonas to a friend. Say one thing you are looking forward to and one thing you are glad about because it makes the trip easier.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the message against criteria audience-and-purpose, both-perspectives, source-facts, expression-choice, and reflexive-agreement. All listed criteria are gating.

criteria.instruction: Is a message from Sara or Jonas to a friend about the station situation.
Communicates one anticipated experience, using glede seg til, and appreciation of one existing fact, using være glad for.
Uses details supplied in the station update without contradicting them.
Uses glede seg til for the anticipated experience and være glad for for the existing fact.
Uses a reflexive pronoun that agrees with the message writer’s subject.

prompt.value: Message to the study group: «Jeg blander uttrykkene for å se fram til noe og for å sette pris på noe som allerede er sant.» Reply in Norwegian. Explain the difference and give one example of each expression: «glede seg til» and «være glad for».

payload.judge_prompt: Kontroller svaret mot kriteriene distinction, two-examples. Begge kriteriene er avgjørende for godkjenning.

criteria.instruction: Forklarer at den ene betydningen gjelder forventning, mens den andre gjelder å sette pris på noe som allerede er sant.
Gir ett norsk eksempel på forventning med «glede seg til» og ett norsk eksempel på å sette pris på noe med «være glad for».

prompt.value: Fill in the correct form of «glede seg til»: «Vi ___ filmen.»

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against criterion completion. Accept «gleder oss til» and capitalization variants.

criteria.instruction: Supplies gleder oss til so the sentence expresses anticipation and agrees with vi.

prompt.value: Choose the reply that fits both facts.

options.why: This contradicts the update that the concert was cancelled.

options.text: Liv gleder seg til å få pengene tilbake.
options.why: This treats an already completed refund as something still anticipated.

options.text: Liv er glad for at hun fikk pengene tilbake.
options.why: The refund has already happened and is the fact Liv appreciates.
